messages.author: c82e7d89d213881d
messages.subject: incomplete beta function
parts:
Hi -- I'm trying to use the incomplete beta function in rstan, and am confused exactly how to do that. I thought I could just call "ibeta", but when I compile I get the error message:

no matches for function name="ibeta"
    arg 0 type=real
    arg 1 type=real
    arg 2 type=real

Any help would be much appreciated!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] incomplete beta function
parts:
There is no incomplete beta in the Stan language --- we use
it on the back end in the C++.

Michael --- could we or should we expose it?

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] incomplete beta function
parts:
I'm not sure if we have the primitives to support it directly
or if it would be a good idea if we did.

What did you need it for?

One possibility is to build a custom version --- the change to
add it is only a couple minutes work, but then Stan and RStan
need to be rebuilt on top of that.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] incomplete beta function
parts:
On Monday, July 13, 2015 at 3:20:55 PM UTC-4, Sharad Goel wrote:
Any chance there's a workaround for using ibeta before it's officially exposed (e.g., via user-defined functions)?

beta_cdf(x, a, b) * exp(lbeta(a,b));

But maybe beta_cdf() is not that stable ...

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] incomplete beta function
parts:
I think the stability of beta_cdf() is waiting on the
patches to ibeta that Michael made for 2.7. So it may
work, but should be better in 2.7.

- Bob
